preamble: Devoicing of the voiced velar stop [ɡ] to [k] is one of the most widespread consonant changes. It occurs as a regular historical shift (Grimm's law, PIE *g > Proto-Germanic *k), as the general loss of voiced initials in most Chinese varieties (Middle Chinese *ɡ- > k-/kʰ-, with the former voicing surviving as the yang tone register), and as final-obstruent devoicing in German and Russian.

examples.note: Grimm's law devoiced the PIE plain voiced stops: *g > *k.
The Middle Chinese voiced initial devoiced to unaspirated [k]; Shanghainese /ɡoŋ²³/ keeps the voiced initial. The lost voicing is reflected in the low (yang) tone category.
Final obstruent devoicing (Auslautverhärtung) in the standard language of Germany and Austria.
Word-final devoicing of /ɡ/; southern Russian varieties have [drux] instead.
Itunyoso lost all voiced stops; Chicahuaxtla and Copala keep gãʔ. The labialized *gw likewise became kw, as in *gwii 'day, sun' > kwi.
Konso devoiced the Proto-East Cushitic voiced stops *b, *d, *g to /p, t, k/.

examples.from: Old Khmer គង៑ gaṅ 'to remain'
examples.note: Middle Khmer devoicing of Old Khmer /ɡ/; the following vowel carries the high-register reflex of the former voiced onset.

examples.from: Old Khmer គាប៑ gāp 'to be good, fitting'
